protocol.name: cupertino_global_shortcuts_v1

description.summary: the shortcuts applications use while another one has the keyboard

protocol.description: The desktop portal's backend binds the shortcuts the person allowed an application through the GlobalShortcuts portal. The server takes a bound chord before the focused client sees it and tells the backend when it goes down and up; the focused client gets neither the press nor the release. The protocol is private and unstable: interfaces may change without a version bump.

interface.name: cupertino_global_shortcuts_v1

description.summary: the chords of the portal's shortcuts

interface.description:
Global singleton, offered only to the portal process the server started on a connection of its own. Right after binding, and again whenever the server's own key bindings change, the server sends one reserved event for each chord it keeps for itself, followed by done; each group replaces the previous one. A chord the server keeps never reaches a shortcut bound here, whatever was bound.
A bound chord fires only while the session is unlocked, no application holds the keyboard shortcuts and no switcher is open; then it goes to this object, never to the focused client. Destroying the object, or the connection ending, unbinds every shortcut it bound.

request.name: bind
unbind
request.description: The shortcut `id` no longer takes its chord. An id that is not bound is ignored.

description.summary: a chord the server keeps for itself
end of a group of reserved events

event.name: pressed

description.summary: the chord of a shortcut went down

event.description: Sent once for a press; the key's repeats send nothing.

arg.name: time
arg.summary: the key event's time in milliseconds

event.name: released

description.summary: the key of a pressed shortcut went up

event.description: Sent once for each pressed, when the key that pressed it is released, even if the shortcut was unbound in between.

arg.name: time
arg.summary: the key event's time in milliseconds
